blocks.text: SDG 7 seeks to ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all. Within the higher-education context, research plays an important role in developing clean-energy technologies, improving energy efficiency, supporting renewable-energy integration and generating knowledge for sustainable energy transitions.

Kalinga University's Scopus-indexed research demonstrates multidisciplinary engagement with these objectives through studies involving renewable energy, solar photovoltaics, energy-storage systems, electric mobility, smart-grid technologies, microgrids, bioenergy and sustainable energy management.
The increasing number of potentially SDG 7-aligned Scopus publications, particularly during 2024–2025, indicates strengthening research activity in clean and sustainable energy domains.

Research Theme Distribution

Kalinga University's SDG 7 research encompasses diverse areas of clean and renewable energy, with Solar and Photovoltaic Energy (81 outputs) emerging as the leading research theme, followed by Smart Grid, Microgrid & Power Systems (60 outputs) and Other Energy Research (59 outputs). Additional contributions include electric vehicles, energy storage, bioenergy, energy efficiency, and sustainability. This multidisciplinary research engagement reflects the University's commitment to advancing clean-energy technologies, sustainable energy management, and renewable energy innovation.
Major Research Contributions

Kalinga University’s clean energy research portfolio includes work on lead-free and organic perovskite solar cells, performance improvement of photovoltaic systems, solar tracking, grid-connected PV systems, microgrid stability, smart electricity monitoring, electric vehicle charging systems, hybrid energy storage, battery technologies, biofuels and bioethanol, and artificial intelligence-driven power management.

The titles screened indicate relevance to both technology development and applied sustainability. For example, research on solar cell performance and perovskite materials contributes to renewable energy generation; microgrid and smart-grid studies support energy reliability; EV charging and battery management research supports low-carbon transport; and biofuel/biomass studies support alternative clean energy pathways.

sections.title: 7.2 University Measures Towards Affordable and Clean Energy

blocks.text: 7.2.1 Energy-Efficient Renovation and Building

Kalinga University is committed to developing and maintaining an energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable campus through the adoption of green infrastructure and energy conservation practices. The University integrates energy efficiency considerations into the planning, construction, renovation, and operation of campus buildings to minimize energy consumption, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and promote responsible use of natural resources. Sustainable infrastructure development is guided by the University's commitment to environmental stewardship and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy.

The University has installed a 300 kWp Solar Power Plant, which contributes significantly to meeting the campus's electricity requirements through clean and renewable energy. The plant has generated 125,946.60 kWh of electricity, reducing dependence on conventional grid power and lowering carbon emissions. In addition, a biogas plant has been established to convert biodegradable organic waste into renewable energy, supporting efficient waste management while producing an alternative source of clean fuel.

To further enhance energy efficiency, Kalinga University has implemented sensor-based LED lighting systems in various academic and administrative buildings. These systems automatically regulate lighting based on occupancy, thereby minimizing unnecessary electricity consumption and improving overall energy performance. The University also promotes the use of energy-efficient electrical equipment and encourages periodic maintenance of electrical systems to optimize operational efficiency.

Energy conservation is complemented by a range of awareness and capacity-building initiatives. The University regularly observes National Energy Conservation Day and organizes awareness campaigns, workshops, seminars, poster competitions, technical exhibitions, and student-led projects focusing on renewable energy, energy-efficient technologies, and sustainable infrastructure. Faculty members and students actively undertake research on improving solar photovoltaic performance, hybrid renewable energy systems, and smart energy management solutions, contributing to the development of innovative and sustainable energy practices.

Recognizing the importance of developing a skilled workforce for the clean energy sector, Kalinga University also conducts a Free Solar PV Installation Helper Training Programme under the Green Jobs Sector (NSQF Level 4). The programme equips participants with practical skills in solar photovoltaic installation and maintenance, enhancing employability while supporting India's transition towards renewable energy.

Through the integration of renewable energy infrastructure, energy-efficient technologies, sustainable campus operations, research, and skill development initiatives, Kalinga University demonstrates its strong commitment to creating an energy-efficient campus and advancing the objectives of SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy.
7.2.2 Upgrade Buildings to Higher Energy Efficiency
Building Energy Efficiency Upgrade Plan at Kalinga University

Kalinga University is committed to continuously improving the energy performance of its campus infrastructure through the adoption of energy-efficient technologies, renewable energy integration, and sustainable building management practices. In line with its commitment to Sustainable Development Goal 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), the University has implemented several measures to reduce electricity consumption, improve operational efficiency, and minimize its environmental footprint while providing a comfortable learning and working environment.
The University's energy efficiency strategy is based on the following key principles:

Energy-Efficient Infrastructure: Adoption of energy-saving technologies such as sensor-based LED lighting systems, energy-efficient electrical equipment, and optimized building services to reduce electricity consumption across academic, administrative, residential, and common facilities.

Renewable Energy Integration: Maximizing the use of clean energy through the installation and efficient utilization of a 300 kWp rooftop Solar Power Plant, supported by renewable energy initiatives such as the campus biogas plant to reduce dependence on conventional grid electricity.

Continuous Monitoring and Improvement: Regular monitoring of electricity consumption, renewable energy generation, and maintenance of electrical infrastructure to enhance overall energy performance and identify opportunities for further improvement.

As part of its energy conservation efforts, Kalinga University has installed sensor-based LED lighting systems throughout the campus. These systems automatically control lighting based on occupancy, significantly reducing unnecessary electricity usage while lowering operational costs. The University also encourages the use of energy-efficient appliances and periodically upgrades electrical systems to improve performance and reliability.

Kalinga University's 300 kWp Solar Power Plant contributes to sustainable campus operations by generating clean and renewable electricity. During 2024–25, the solar power plant generated 93,936.10 kWh of electricity, equivalent to 338.17 Gigajoules (GJ). This renewable energy generation helps reduce dependence on conventional grid electricity and supports the University's efforts to minimise greenhouse gas emissions. The University's built-up campus area benefits from these renewable energy and energy conservation initiatives.

To complement renewable energy generation, Kalinga University also operates a biogas plant, which converts biodegradable organic waste into renewable fuel, thereby promoting circular resource management and reducing dependence on conventional energy sources.

The University regularly organizes National Energy Conservation Day, renewable energy awareness campaigns, workshops, seminars, technical exhibitions, poster competitions, and student innovation projects to promote responsible energy consumption and sustainable technologies. Faculty members and students actively undertake research on solar photovoltaic efficiency, hybrid renewable energy systems, smart energy management, and green technologies, supporting continuous improvements in campus sustainability.

Through the integration of renewable energy infrastructure, energy-efficient technologies, continuous monitoring, and future-focused planning, Kalinga University is steadily transforming its campus into a more sustainable and energy-efficient environment. These initiatives reduce operational costs, lower carbon emissions, and reinforce the University's commitment to achieving SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy while serving as a model for sustainable campus development.
7.2.3 Carbon Reduction and Emission Reduction Process

Kalinga University is committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting a low-carbon campus through renewable energy adoption, energy-efficient infrastructure, sustainable waste management, and environmental awareness initiatives. As part of its commitment to Sustainable Development Goal 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and broader environmental sustainability goals, the University continuously implements measures to minimize its carbon footprint while promoting responsible resource utilization across the campus.

A key component of Kalinga University's carbon reduction strategy is the adoption of renewable energy infrastructure. The University operates a 300 kWp Solar Power Plant, which contributes to clean electricity generation and reduces dependence on conventional grid electricity. During 2024–25, the solar power plant generated 93,936.10 kWh of renewable electricity, equivalent to 338.17 Gigajoules (GJ). This renewable energy generation supports the University's efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with electricity consumption, promote energy efficiency, and strengthen environmentally sustainable campus operations.

To further improve energy efficiency and reduce indirect emissions, Kalinga University has installed sensor-based LED lighting systems across academic, administrative, and residential buildings. These systems optimize electricity usage by automatically controlling lighting based on occupancy, thereby reducing unnecessary energy consumption and associated greenhouse gas emissions.

The University also promotes sustainable waste-to-energy practices through the operation of a biogas plant, where biodegradable organic waste is converted into renewable fuel. This initiative not only provides an alternative source of clean energy but also minimizes methane emissions from organic waste disposal while supporting effective campus waste management.

Kalinga University complements these infrastructure initiatives with extensive environmental awareness and capacity-building programmes. The University regularly organizes National Energy Conservation Day, renewable energy awareness campaigns, workshops, seminars, poster competitions, technical exhibitions, and student-led innovation projects to encourage energy conservation and climate-responsible behaviour among students, faculty, staff, and the surrounding community. Faculty members and students actively undertake research on renewable energy technologies, solar photovoltaic efficiency, hybrid energy systems, and smart energy management, contributing to long-term carbon reduction solutions.

The University's commitment to green skills development is further reflected through its Free Solar PV Installation Helper Training Programme (NSQF Level 4) under the Green Jobs Sector, which prepares skilled professionals capable of supporting India's transition towards clean and renewable energy technologies.
Key Carbon Reduction Measures Implemented by Kalinga University
Installation and operation of a 300 kWp Solar Power Plant for renewable electricity generation.
Use of sensor-based LED lighting systems to reduce electricity consumption.
Operation of a biogas plant for converting biodegradable waste into clean energy.
Promotion of renewable energy research, innovation, and student projects.
Organization of energy conservation campaigns, workshops, seminars, and awareness programmes.
Skill development through Solar PV Installation Helper Training to promote green employment and clean energy adoption.

Through the integration of renewable energy generation, energy-efficient technologies, sustainable waste management, environmental education, and green skill development, Kalinga University continues to strengthen its carbon reduction efforts and contribute towards a cleaner, more sustainable, and climate-resilient campus, supporting the objectives of SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy as well as India's commitment to sustainable development and climate action.
7.2.4 Plan to Reduce Energy Consumption
Energy Consumption Reduction Plan at Kalinga University

Kalinga University has developed a comprehensive strategy to reduce overall campus energy consumption by integrating renewable energy, adopting energy-efficient technologies, promoting sustainable operational practices, and encouraging responsible energy use among all stakeholders. The University's plan aligns with its commitment to Sustainable Development Goal 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and supports its vision of developing a sustainable, energy-efficient, and environmentally responsible campus.
Objectives
Kalinga University aims to promote sustainable energy management and improve energy efficiency across its campus through the following objectives:
Reduce overall electricity consumption through energy-efficient infrastructure and sustainable operational practices.
Increase the utilisation of renewable energy to reduce dependence on conventional electricity sources.
Encourage responsible energy consumption among students, faculty members, staff, and visitors.
Strengthen energy management through regular monitoring, maintenance, and continuous improvement.
Promote research, innovation, and skill development in renewable energy and energy conservation technologies.
Current Energy Scenario

Kalinga University's major energy-consuming facilities include academic and administrative buildings, laboratories, computer centres, student hostels, residential facilities, libraries, auditoriums, water pumping systems, campus lighting, air-conditioning, ventilation, and other electrical equipment.

To promote sustainable energy utilisation, the University operates a 300 kWp Solar Power Plant, which generated 93,936.10 kWh of renewable electricity (equivalent to 338.17 Gigajoules) during the 2024–25 reporting period. This renewable energy generation contributes to reducing dependence on conventional grid electricity and supports the University's carbon reduction initiatives.

Additionally, the University operates a biogas plant that converts biodegradable organic waste into renewable fuel, promoting sustainable waste management and alternative energy utilisation. The adoption of sensor-based LED lighting, energy-efficient electrical systems, and regular maintenance practices further supports energy conservation across campus facilities.
These initiatives demonstrate Kalinga University's continued efforts to improve energy efficiency, promote renewable energy utilisation, and maintain environmentally responsible campus operations.
Strategic Action Plan
1. Energy Monitoring and Management

The University periodically reviews electricity consumption and renewable energy generation to identify opportunities for improving energy efficiency. Regular maintenance of electrical systems and monitoring of solar power generation help optimize overall campus energy performance.
Future initiatives include:
Conducting periodic energy audits.
Maintaining records of electricity consumption and renewable energy generation.
Developing digital monitoring systems for energy performance analysis.
Promoting data-driven decision-making for energy conservation.
2. Energy-Efficient Infrastructure
Kalinga University continues to upgrade campus infrastructure through:
Installation of sensor-based LED lighting systems across academic and administrative buildings.
Replacement of conventional lighting with high-efficiency LED fixtures.
Use of energy-efficient electrical equipment wherever feasible.
Regular preventive maintenance of electrical installations to minimize energy losses.
Future upgrades will include smart lighting controls, automated energy management systems, and adoption of high-efficiency electrical appliances.

blocks.text: Monitoring and Expected Outcomes

The University will continue to monitor electricity consumption, renewable energy generation, and the performance of energy-efficient systems through periodic reviews. The effectiveness of energy conservation initiatives will be evaluated using indicators such as electricity consumption trends, renewable energy generation, operational cost savings, and reduced dependence on conventional grid electricity.

Through these initiatives, Kalinga University aims to continuously improve campus energy efficiency, expand the use of renewable energy, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and strengthen its contribution towards SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy, while creating a sustainable learning environment for future generations.
7.2.5 Energy Wastage Identification
Energy Wastage Identification and Mitigation at Kalinga University

Kalinga University follows a systematic approach to identify areas of unnecessary energy consumption and implement corrective measures that improve overall energy efficiency across the campus. The University recognizes that minimizing energy wastage is essential for reducing operational costs, conserving natural resources, and achieving the objectives of Sustainable Development Goal 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy).
Objectives
The University's energy wastage identification programme aims to:
Identify major sources of unnecessary electricity consumption.
Improve the efficiency of campus infrastructure and electrical systems.
Promote responsible energy use among students, faculty, and staff.
Reduce operational costs through energy conservation.
Support continuous improvement in sustainable campus management.
Methodology
Energy wastage is identified through a combination of:
Periodic monitoring of campus electricity consumption.
Inspection of lighting systems, electrical equipment, and renewable energy installations.
Regular maintenance of electrical infrastructure.
Observation of operational practices across academic, residential, and administrative facilities.
Feedback from departments, facility management personnel, and campus users regarding energy consumption patterns.
Key Areas of Energy Wastage and Corrective Measures
1. Lighting Systems
Identified Issues
Unnecessary operation of lights in unoccupied areas.
Use of conventional lighting in selected locations.
Corrective Measures
Installation of sensor-based LED lighting systems.
Replacement of conventional lighting with energy-efficient LED fixtures.
Promotion of responsible lighting practices across campus.
2. Electrical Equipment
Identified Issues
Idle operation of computers and electrical appliances.
Use of outdated equipment with higher power consumption.
Corrective Measures
Procurement of energy-efficient electrical equipment.
Regular maintenance of electrical appliances.
Encouraging users to switch off equipment when not in use.
3. Renewable Energy Systems
Identified Issues
Performance loss due to dust accumulation and routine wear.
Corrective Measures
Periodic maintenance and cleaning of the 300 kWp Solar Power Plant.
Continuous monitoring of renewable electricity generation.
Performance optimization through regular inspections.
4. Laboratory and Academic Facilities
Identified Issues
Continuous operation of laboratory equipment beyond operational requirements.
Corrective Measures
Scheduled use of laboratory equipment.
Proper shutdown procedures after laboratory sessions.
Awareness among laboratory staff regarding energy conservation.
5. Campus Utilities
Identified Issues
Energy consumption associated with water pumping and common utility services.
Corrective Measures
Preventive maintenance of pumping systems.
Efficient scheduling of utility operations.
Promotion of water conservation practices to reduce energy demand.
6. Behavioural Energy Conservation
Kalinga University recognizes that behavioural changes significantly contribute to reducing energy consumption. The University regularly conducts:
National Energy Conservation Day celebrations.
Renewable energy awareness campaigns.
Workshops, seminars, and guest lectures.
Poster competitions and student projects.
Faculty and student engagement programmes on sustainable energy practices.

These initiatives encourage the campus community to adopt simple yet effective energy-saving habits, including switching off unused lights and equipment, minimizing unnecessary electricity consumption, and promoting responsible use of renewable energy resources.
Continuous Improvement

The University continuously reviews its energy conservation practices and upgrades infrastructure wherever feasible. Future initiatives include expanding smart energy monitoring systems, increasing renewable energy capacity, introducing automated energy management technologies, and strengthening campus-wide awareness programmes.

Through regular identification of energy wastage, implementation of corrective measures, and active participation of the University community, Kalinga University continues to improve its energy efficiency and reinforce its commitment to sustainable campus development under SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy.

blocks.text: Sustainable Investment and Clean Energy Commitment

Kalinga University is committed to promoting environmental sustainability by prioritizing investments in renewable energy infrastructure, energy-efficient technologies, and sustainable campus development. While the University's primary focus is on expanding clean energy adoption rather than investing in carbon-intensive infrastructure, its sustainability initiatives reflect a long-term commitment to reducing dependence on conventional energy sources and promoting responsible resource utilization.

The University has invested in a 300 kWp Solar Power Plant, which serves as a major source of renewable electricity for campus operations. Continuous improvements in energy-efficient infrastructure, including the installation of sensor-based LED lighting systems and a biogas plant for renewable energy generation from biodegradable waste, further demonstrate the University's commitment to sustainable development.

Future infrastructure development and campus modernization initiatives continue to emphasize renewable energy technologies, energy-efficient equipment, and environmentally responsible practices. Through these measures, Kalinga University aligns its institutional development with the objectives of SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy, supporting India's transition towards a cleaner and more sustainable energy future.

Kalinga University, Raipur, regularly monitors renewable energy generation and campus energy performance to improve operational efficiency and promote sustainable energy utilisation. The University has a total built-up area of approximately 829,921 sq. ft. (77,102 m²) and operates a 300 kWp Solar Power Plant to support its renewable energy requirements.
During the 2024–25 reporting period, the solar power plant generated 93,936.10 kWh of renewable electricity, equivalent to 338.17 Gigajoules (GJ).
Calculation of Renewable Energy Generation Density
Annual Renewable Electricity Generated (2024–25) = 93,936.10 kWh
Total Built-up Area = 77,102 m²
Renewable Energy Generation Density = Annual Renewable Electricity Generated ÷ Total Built-up Area
= 1.22 kWh/m²/year
Conversion into Gigajoules (GJ):
= 0.00439 GJ/m²/year

The renewable energy generation density of 1.22 kWh/m²/year (0.00439 GJ/m²/year) reflects the University's solar electricity generation relative to its built-up campus area. Through renewable energy utilisation, energy-efficient infrastructure, and regular monitoring of electricity generation, Kalinga University continues to strengthen sustainable campus operations and reduce its dependence on conventional energy sources.
7.4.1 Community Outreach for Energy Efficiency

Kalinga University actively promotes awareness of renewable energy, energy conservation, and sustainable development among students, faculty, school students, and the wider community. The University regularly organizes National Energy Conservation Day, renewable energy awareness programmes, workshops, seminars, guest lectures, technical exhibitions, poster competitions, and outreach activities to encourage responsible energy consumption and environmental stewardship.

As part of its commitment to green skill development, the University conducts a Free Solar PV Installation Helper Training Programme (NSQF Level 4) under the Green Jobs Sector. The programme equips participants with practical knowledge and technical skills in solar photovoltaic installation and maintenance, creating employment opportunities while promoting wider adoption of renewable energy technologies.
These initiatives contribute to increasing public awareness of clean energy solutions and support India's transition towards sustainable and affordable energy.

blocks.text: 7.4.2 Promotion of Renewable Energy
Kalinga University actively promotes the adoption of renewable energy through campus infrastructure, academic programmes, research activities, and community engagement initiatives.
The University's renewable energy initiatives include:
Installation of a 300 kWp Solar Power Plant.
Operation of a campus biogas plant.
Renewable energy awareness campaigns.
National Energy Conservation Day celebrations.
Solar PV skill development programmes.
Student projects on renewable energy technologies.
Faculty research on solar photovoltaic systems, hybrid renewable energy systems, and smart energy management.
Through these initiatives, the University encourages students and the wider community to adopt sustainable energy practices and contributes towards India's renewable energy goals.

7.4.3 Energy Efficiency Services for Industry
Kalinga University contributes to capacity building in renewable energy by offering training programmes, academic research, and technical education in clean energy technologies.

The Solar PV Installation Helper Training Programme (NSQF Level 4) prepares participants with practical skills required by the renewable energy industry, thereby supporting the development of a skilled workforce for solar energy installation and maintenance.

Faculty members and students also undertake research and innovation projects related to renewable energy technologies, smart energy management, and solar photovoltaic performance, creating opportunities for future academic-industry collaboration in sustainable energy solutions.

blocks.text: Kalinga University promotes the development and adoption of clean energy technologies through academic research, innovation, training programmes, and institutional sustainability initiatives.
Research undertaken by faculty members and students focuses on:

Hybrid renewable energy systems.

Sustainable energy technologies.

The University integrates these activities with awareness programmes, technical exhibitions, and skill development initiatives, encouraging wider adoption of renewable energy technologies within society.
Through these efforts, Kalinga University contributes to knowledge generation and supports national priorities for clean and sustainable energy development.
7.4.5 Assistance to Low-Carbon Innovation

Kalinga University encourages innovation and research in renewable energy and sustainable technologies through interdisciplinary research projects, student innovation activities, technical exhibitions, and project-based learning.
Faculty members and students actively work on:
Solar photovoltaic efficiency enhancement.
Hybrid renewable energy systems.
Smart energy management.
Green technologies.

The University also promotes entrepreneurship and employability in the renewable energy sector through its Solar PV skill development programme, creating opportunities for future innovation in low-carbon technologies.
7.5.1 Low-Carbon Energy Use

Kalinga University, Raipur, promotes the utilisation of low-carbon energy sources to reduce dependence on conventional electricity and support sustainable campus operations. The University's renewable energy infrastructure includes a 300 kWp Solar Power Plant and a biogas plant, contributing to clean energy generation, sustainable waste management, and greenhouse gas emission reduction.

During the 2024–25 reporting period, the University's solar power plant generated 93,936.10 kWh of renewable electricity, equivalent to 338.17 Gigajoules (GJ). This renewable energy generation helps reduce dependence on grid-supplied electricity and supports the University's efforts towards environmentally responsible energy consumption.
Renewable Energy Generation (2024–25)

rows.text: Solar Power Plant (300 kWp)

blocks.text: In addition to solar electricity generation, the University operates a biogas plant that converts biodegradable organic waste into renewable fuel, supporting sustainable waste utilisation and alternative energy production. The University also promotes energy conservation through sensor-based LED lighting, energy-efficient electrical systems, and awareness initiatives.
Through these measures, Kalinga University continues to strengthen its low-carbon energy practices, improve renewable energy utilisation, and support environmentally sustainable campus operations.
